title.narrative: Support to Strategic Note of UN Women Albania 2022-2026
Support to the Strategic Note UN Women 2022-2026 Albania

description.narrative:
The overall objective of the Strategic Note of UN Women in Albania 2022-20206 is:
All women and girls fully enjoy and exercise their human rights in a gender equal society and meaningfully contribute to Albania's sustainable and inclusive socio-economic development and EU integration.

NDetta är ett icke öronmärkt stöd till den strategiska rapporten från UN Women i Albanien 2022–2026. De tre huvudinriktningarna i den strategiska planen är: 1) Rättvisa investeringar i människor; 2) Produktiv utveckling för alla. 3) Jämställdhetsmedveten styrning. UN Women arbetar med partners för att bekämpa könsstereotyper, bland annat genom medier, medvetandehöjande åtgärder och kapacitetsuppbyggnad. På lokal nivå stöder UN Women det civila samhället, tjänsteleverantörer, lokalsamhällen och personal vid lokala myndigheter. På central nivå arbetar UN Women med flera fackministerier, statistiska institut (INSTAT), parlamentsledamöter, statens högsta revisionsorgan, nationella institutioner för mänskliga rättigheter, civilsamhällesorganisationer, den akademiska världen, den privata sektorn, media och andra. Inom ramen för dessa engagemang erbjuder UN Women kunskap, tekniskt stöd, policyrådgivning och exponering för bästa praxis globalt och från regionen om alla aspekter av jämställdhetsagendan.

This is un-earmarked support to the Strategic Note of UN Women in Albania 2022-2026. The three main directions of the Strategic Plan are: 1) Equitable investment in People; 2) Productive and Inclusive Development; 3) Gender Responsive Governance. UN Women works with partners to tackle gender stereotypes, including through media, awareness raising and building capacities. At local level, UN Women supports civil society, service providers, communities and staff of local governments. At the central level, UN Women works with several line ministries, statistical institute (INSTAT), members of Parliament, State Supreme Audit, National Human Rights Institutions, civil society organizations, academia, the private sector, media and others. Across these engagements, UN Women offers knowledge, technical support, policy advice and exposure to best practices globally and from the region on all aspects of the gender equality agenda.

Agreement UN Women Albania Strategic Note

description.narrative:
Key results 2025
Outcome 1: More Equitable Investment in People Local governments increasingly adopted inclusive, evidence-based planning and participatory budgeting processes, resulting in public investments that better addressed the needs of women and marginalized groups. UN Women supported this shift by promoting gender-responsive and disability-inclusive service models, strengthening data collection for local planning, and advancing innovative work on the care economy through research, policy analysis, toolkits, and training materials.
Outcome 2: More Inclusive and Sustainable Development Gender equality became more integrated into economic development initiatives, especially in tourism and rural value chains in northern Albania. Women increased their participation in entrepreneurship and income-generating activities, supported by initiatives such as the annual EXPO. UN Women contributed through gender-sensitive research, integrated programming, multi-stakeholder partnerships, and pilot work on climate change and the green economy, creating new opportunities for women entrepreneurs and rural women.
Outcome 3: Stronger Gender-Responsive Governance Albania strengthened its legal and institutional framework for gender equality, including adopting the Gender Equality Law (2025) and advancing reforms on violence against women. Gender-responsive budgeting, policy-making, and service delivery improved, while coordination among government, civil society, and development partners increased. UN Women provided technical leadership, evidence-based policy support, and coordination mechanisms. In 2025, it supported 14 municipalities in developing Local Gender Action Plans and further strengthened gender-responsive budgeting and accountability systems in line with EU standards and SDG commitments.
Organizational Performance UN Women Albania enhanced its organizational effectiveness by strengthening communications, results-based management, coordination, and knowledge management. Flexible funding improved delivery and accountability, while expanded partnerships, particularly with the private sector, and successful resource mobilization reinforced the Country Offices role as a key partner in advancing gender equality reforms.
